review.notes: Drafted for #11. The polygon is the sector as established on D-Day (where the assault actually landed), not as planned. Geometry derivation: Map VII of Utah Beach to Cherbourg (Commons scan, 1844x1142 px) has a 500-yard scale bar (163 px, so about 2.8 m per pixel) and a north arrow. On it, Uncle Red and Tare Green as established on D-Day meet at the Exit 2 road, Uncle Red running about 266 px (about 750 m) south of it and Tare Green about 263 px (about 740 m) north. As planned, Uncle Red ran from 424 px to 752 px and Tare Green from 752 px to 1122 px north of Exit 2. Exit 2 (Causeway 2, towards Sainte-Marie-du-Mont) was matched to the present-day D913, which meets the coast road at -1.17687, 49.4151; that point was projected onto the present-day OSM coastline and the map distances were laid off along the coastline from there. Seaward depth is the distance from the high-water mark to the low-water mark measured on Map VII at each sector boundary (about 0.8 to 1.4 km), applied perpendicular to the general line of the coast (bearing 319 degrees). Cross-check: Map VII's Exit 3 road, transformed the same way, falls within about 80 m of the point where the present-day D67 meets the coast. Accuracy is "approximate" because the 1944 map was georeferenced by hand from one road junction, a scale bar and the modern coastline, and the 1944 high- and low-water lines are not today's. Company and wave allocations for tanks and engineers come from Map VII, which shows the landing plan as of 24 May 1944; Wikipedia confirms the rifle companies landed as planned on each beach, but no readable source says whether the tank and engineer detachments landed on the beach the plan gave them. Books Wikipedia cites (Ford & Zaloga 2009; Balkoski 2005) could not be read; see utah-beach.json for the hosts that were refused. Sources checked 2026-11-28 by an independent check-sources agent for PR #21: every Wikipedia quote matched against the rendered text of the pinned revisions (Utah Beach 1372907065, Normandy landings 1386946425) in its cited section; Map VII (Commons File:Utah_beach.jpg, page revision 913116035) read directly, and its wave table, legend, scale bar (500 yd = 163 px) and sector brackets confirmed; Wikidata Q18380084, Q3159110 and Q108628156 statements confirmed; polygons re-measured against OSM coastline and roads from the OpenFreeMap tiles (planet build 20261122): landward vertices lie on the coastline, the D913 ends at the stated junction, D67 lies about 1.84 km up the coast from Exit 2, against about 1.78 km to Exit 3 on Map VII, and seaward depths agree with Map VII to within about 100 m.

summary.text: The right-hand (northern) of the two assault beaches at Utah. As planned, Tare Green lay opposite the strongpoint at Les Dunes de Varreville, but currents carried the landing craft south and the beach was established north of Exit 2 instead. Companies B and C of the 8th Infantry landed here in the first wave at 06:30 and Companies A and D in the second. Company B moved on strongpoint WN7 near La Madeleine, the headquarters of the 3rd Battalion, 919th Grenadier Regiment, and met little resistance there; Company C put out of action strongpoint WN5 at La Grande Dune, which the preliminary bombardment had badly damaged.
